title: The Bell That Rang at Low Tide
summary: When celebrated harbor engineer Alaric Venn vanishes during the unveiling of Tideglass Quay, the city’s new floodgate project is thrown into scandal. Moments before his disappearance, the old chapel bell rings through fog from a locked, condemned tower. SirLocked and his companion must separate civic pageantry from hidden grudges, test witness accounts against physical evidence, and uncover whether Venn was taken, fled, or met with something more sinister.

characters.name: Maribel Quince
characters.description: Ambitious, controlled, and publicly devoted to the Tideglass Quay opening. A scandal could ruin her career, which makes her both helpful and guarded.

characters.name: Jonah Pike
characters.description: A salt-stiffened veteran of underwater salvage who speaks in omens but notices practical details others miss. His old quarrels with harbor engineers make him an easy suspect.

characters.name: Celia Venn
characters.description: Sharp, wounded, and more informed than she first admits. She argued with Alaric over a sealed family ledger shortly before he disappeared.

characters.name: Tomas Reed
characters.description: A charming sketch artist assigned to capture the unveiling for the morning edition. He arrived early, drew constantly, and claims his drawings prove he saw nothing unusual.

characters.name: Edda Krail
characters.description: Keeper of the condemned chapel’s keys and habits. She resents the city’s neglect of the tower and insists no living hand could have entered it without her knowing.

items.name: Cracked Pocket Compass
items.description: A brass pocket compass found on the unveiling platform where Venn had stood.
items.inspectText: The glass is cracked inward, the needle is pinned at an odd angle, and a tiny flake of blue sealing wax is caught beneath the hinge.

items.name: Weatherproof Sketchbook
items.description: Tomas Reed’s oilskin-bound sketchbook, recovered from a paint-stained crate in the newspaper loft.
items.inspectText: The pages are damp at the corners but intact. Several drawings are dated with precise times in a neat illustrator’s hand.

clues.title: Compass Cracked Inward
clues.content: Venn’s compass was not dropped from a height; its glass was crushed by a hard edge pressing down on it. A fleck of blue sealing wax is trapped beneath the hinge.
clues.visualDescription: A brass pocket compass lies open on the wet platform boards, its cracked glass catching fog-diffused light.
clues.inventoryDescription: Cracked compass with inward damage and a blue wax fleck in the hinge.
clues.narrativeMeaning: Venn was forced or knocked against something close at hand on the platform, and the blue wax connects the disappearance to a prepared object rather than a spontaneous flight.

clues.title: Scratched Certification Sentence
clues.content: Venn’s ceremonial speech has one sentence violently scratched out: 'I cannot certify the western sluice under present workmanship.'
clues.visualDescription: A rain-speckled speech page is pinned beneath a silver paperknife, with one line gouged through so hard the paper is torn.
clues.inventoryDescription: Speech page with a destroyed sentence refusing to certify the western sluice.
clues.narrativeMeaning: Venn was preparing to expose a problem with Tideglass Quay, giving several people a reason to silence or control him before he spoke.

clues.title: Blue Wax on the Platform Rail
clues.content: A smear of blue sealing wax is pressed into the underside of the platform rail beside the press pen, shaped like it once held a small wire or cord in place.
clues.visualDescription: Beneath a varnished rail, a thumb-sized blue wax smear glistens where rain has not washed it away.
clues.inventoryDescription: Blue wax smear with a narrow groove, found under the platform rail near the press position.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The wax was used as a temporary fastener for a prepared mechanism near where the press had access, not merely as an official seal.

clues.title: Salt-Wet Bell Rope
clues.content: The chapel bell rope is wet with brine, not rain, and tied with a recent rolling hitch around a thinner cord descending into an old drain channel.
clues.visualDescription: A thick, frayed bell rope hangs beside the stair, darkened with saltwater at the knot while the surrounding floor remains dusty.
clues.inventoryDescription: Brine-wet bell rope tied to a thinner cord that runs down into the drainage masonry.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The bell was rung remotely through the tower’s drainage route, making the locked tower a trick rather than a miracle.

clues.title: Fresh Brass Pulley Filings
clues.content: New brass filings lie beneath an old beam where a small removable pulley has recently scored the wood. The chapel’s original fittings are iron, not brass.
clues.visualDescription: A dusty beam bears a bright crescent scratch, with gold-colored filings sprinkled on the rotten stair tread below.
clues.inventoryDescription: Fresh brass filings from a temporary pulley installed in the bell tower.
clues.narrativeMeaning: Someone brought modern gear into the tower, set up a temporary pull system, and removed most of it before the investigation arrived.

clues.title: Old Diver Prints in Tower Dust
clues.content: Heavy boot prints in the tower dust appear to match a diver’s hobnailed soles, but the dust has settled inside the impressions and the edges are softened with age.
clues.visualDescription: Broad, hobnailed footprints cross the dusty chapel floor, dramatic but softened under a grey film of settled dust.
clues.inventoryDescription: Old diver-style boot prints in the chapel tower dust.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The prints tempt suspicion toward Jonah Pike, but their age means they predate the disappearance and cannot explain the fresh bell-ringing trick.

clues.title: Culvert Hatch Beneath the Platform
clues.content: Venn’s revised plan shows an inspection hatch directly under the unveiling platform, linked by a maintenance culvert to the Gull Street warehouses and the unfinished sluice chamber.
clues.visualDescription: A large engineering plan is spread over Venn’s desk, with a red-pencil circle around the platform footprint and a narrow route marked beneath it.
clues.inventoryDescription: Harbor plan showing a hidden hatch and maintenance culvert under the unveiling platform.
clues.narrativeMeaning: Venn did not need to vanish through the crowd; he could have been dropped or forced into a concealed route beneath the platform during the bell distraction.

clues.title: Illustrated Supplement Access Note
clues.content: A Harbor Works ledger records that Tomas Reed requested tower elevations and quay cutaway drawings three weeks earlier for an illustrated newspaper supplement. Edda’s initials approve chapel access for 'sketching only.'
clues.visualDescription: An open ledger page shows neat columns of permit requests, with Tomas Reed’s name beside chapel elevations and Tideglass cutaways.
clues.inventoryDescription: Permit ledger showing Tomas had legitimate early access to chapel and quay plans.
clues.narrativeMeaning: Tomas had the knowledge needed to plan both the bell trick and the underground route before the unveiling.

clues.title: Blue Wax on Warehouse Lock
clues.content: The lock of warehouse C-7 bears the same blue wax, but underneath it is a torn newspaper parcel label rather than a municipal seal.
clues.visualDescription: A black warehouse lock is daubed with blue wax; a scrap of printed parcel paper clings beneath the wax like it was sealed in haste.
clues.inventoryDescription: Blue wax on a Gull Street warehouse lock, mixed with a torn newspaper parcel label.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The blue wax is not exclusively civic property. It links the prepared route to newspaper materials associated with Tomas.

clues.title: Narrow Caster Tracks
clues.content: Twin narrow caster tracks run from the drainage arch to warehouse C-7. Their spacing matches a folding illustrator’s easel-cart, not Jonah’s heavy diver barrow.
clues.visualDescription: In the wet grit, two fine wheel lines curve from a low arch toward the warehouse door, crossing over broader older cart marks.
clues.inventoryDescription: Narrow caster tracks leading from the culvert exit to the warehouse door.
clues.narrativeMeaning: Someone moved a burden from the platform route using a light press or artist’s cart, weakening the theory that a diver dragged Venn away.

clues.title: Caisson Scuffs and Cut Bell Line
clues.content: In the unfinished machine chamber, a cut cord runs from the drainage channel toward Gull Street. Nearby scuffs, a torn cuff button marked A.V., and a half-empty water flask show Venn was held alive here briefly after the platform disappearance.
clues.visualDescription: Beside a tide-black caisson, a frayed cord dangles over fresh boot scuffs, a monogrammed cuff button, and a flask on its side.
clues.inventoryDescription: Cut remote bell line with signs that Alaric Venn was temporarily held in the machine chamber.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The bell mechanism and the abduction route meet below the quay. The culprit used the low-tide drainage path and kept Venn alive long enough to move him onward.

clues.title: The Impossible Sketch
clues.content: Tomas’s sketchbook contains a drawing dated during the public ceremony from inside the condemned bell tower, plus a later page mapping the culvert route to warehouse C-7 before officials announced it. One page is sealed with the same blue wax found on the platform and warehouse lock.
clues.visualDescription: An oilskin sketchbook lies open to a meticulous tower interior view, with a timed note in the margin and blue wax pressed into the page corner.
clues.inventoryDescription: Tomas’s timed sketchbook showing forbidden tower access, the culvert route, and matching blue wax.
clues.narrativeMeaning: Tomas’s own records place him inside the locked tower and in possession of the route before he claimed to know nothing important. It breaks his alibi and ties together the wax, bell trick, and removal path.

dialogues.question: Who had official access to the unveiling platform before the bell rang?
dialogues.answer: Maribel says municipal staff, Venn, and accredited press were allowed on the platform after dawn. She stresses that the crowd ropes were guarded, but admits the press pen stood only a few feet from Venn’s speaking mark.

dialogues.question: Where were you when Venn vanished?
dialogues.answer: Tomas smiles nervously and says he remained in the press pen the entire time, sketching the crowd reaction to the bell. He insists the fog was so thick that he noticed nothing useful.

dialogues.question: Do you recognize the blue wax on the platform rail?
dialogues.answer: Maribel says blue sealing wax is used on Harbor Commission certificates, which makes it look damning for her office. When pressed, she admits the newspapers also received blue-waxed proof bundles for the official illustrated supplement.

dialogues.question: Could anyone have entered the tower without your key?
dialogues.answer: Edda says her tower key never left her belt on the day of the ceremony. However, she remembers permitting Tomas inside weeks earlier to draw the bell and old stair for a newspaper feature.

dialogues.question: Do the tower footprints belong to you?
dialogues.answer: Jonah laughs grimly and says they likely came from an old salvage survey, when half the harbor wore boots like his. He points out that fresh brine on a rope matters more than theatrical old footprints.

dialogues.question: Who would bring brass pulleys into a condemned chapel?
dialogues.answer: Edda says chapel repairs use iron, never bright brass. Brass pocket pulleys are common among stagehands, printers, and illustrators who hang backdrops or drying lines.

dialogues.question: Why would Alaric scratch out his own speech?
dialogues.answer: Celia says Alaric was torn between civic duty and fear. He planned to announce that the western sluice was unsafe, then lost nerve, then changed his mind again. She believes he would not willingly disappear before making the correction.

dialogues.question: Did you know there was a hatch under the platform?
dialogues.answer: Maribel first claims it was boarded over weeks ago. When shown the revised plan, she concedes Venn changed the access route without fully briefing her, which explains her panic but not the bell mechanism.

dialogues.question: What does the access ledger say about Tomas Reed?
dialogues.answer: Celia notes that Tomas had every drawing a careful plotter would need: the chapel elevations, the quay cutaways, and permission to sketch places the public never saw. She also says Alaric thought Tomas was merely a harmless artist.

dialogues.question: Could a diver’s barrow have made the warehouse tracks?
dialogues.answer: Jonah says no. His barrow has wide iron wheels that crush grit flat. The marks by C-7 are too narrow and paired too neatly, like a folding artist’s cart or portable press stand.

dialogues.question: Why is newspaper wrapping caught in the blue wax on warehouse C-7?
dialogues.answer: Tomas says newspapers reuse string, wax, and wrapping by the armful, so the scrap proves nothing. He then adds that he never went near C-7, contradicting the fact that his work materials match the lock and tracks.

dialogues.question: What does the cut cord beneath the quay tell us?
dialogues.answer: Edda identifies the cord’s route as the old chapel drain, long forgotten except by people who studied the tower closely. She says the bell could be made to toll from below when the tide fell enough to leave the drain clear.

dialogues.question: How did your sketchbook show the tower interior during the ceremony?
dialogues.answer: Tomas first calls it a memory sketch, then falters when the timed page shows the bell rope already tied with the remote cord. He cannot explain how he drew a hidden arrangement he claimed never to notice.

dialogues.question: What happens if the evidence is presented now?
dialogues.answer: Maribel says the city will have to halt the opening and search every low-tide chamber. She admits Venn’s warning about the western sluice must be heard, but insists the abduction must be separated from the quay’s engineering scandal.

finalLogic.motive: Tomas Reed abducted Venn out of revenge and zeal for exposure. His father had died years earlier in a harbor works accident that Tomas believed Venn and the Commission minimized, and Venn’s wavering speech convinced Tomas that the truth about Tideglass Quay would again be softened or buried. Tomas meant to force a confession and create a public spectacle that no official could ignore.
finalLogic.method: Weeks before the unveiling, Tomas used his newspaper assignment to access the condemned chapel and the quay plans. He copied the tower route, set a temporary brass pulley and brine-wet cord through the old drain, and arranged for the chapel bell to ring remotely at low tide. On the platform he used blue wax to secure a release cord near the press pen and exploited the bell’s three tolls and fogbound confusion to force Venn through the inspection hatch into the maintenance culvert. Venn was moved by folding easel-cart through Gull Street warehouse C-7 and briefly held in the unfinished caisson chamber. The tower was locked because nobody needed to be inside it when the bell rang.
finalLogic.winEnding: SirLocked reconstructs the route from platform to tower drain, warehouse, and caisson, then confronts Tomas with the impossible sketch. Venn is recovered alive from a low-tide service chamber before the water rises. The quay opening is halted for inspection, Maribel is forced to disclose the unsafe sluice, and the bell’s ghostly toll is revealed as a human scheme built from grief, cleverness, and tide tables.
finalLogic.failEnding: Without the contradiction in Tomas’s sketches, suspicion scatters among Maribel’s civic panic, Jonah’s old diver prints, and Edda’s keys. The city treats the bell as an unsolved marvel, the tide chambers flood before a full search, and the true route of Venn’s disappearance remains hidden beneath Gull Street.
